chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Give scientific reason: Sometimes, higher plants and animals too perform anaerobic respiration.
solution: Higher plants and animals normally respire aerobically, but when the supply of oxygen becomes insufficient, their cells switch to anaerobic respiration to obtain energy. For example, the roots of plants in waterlogged soil and human muscle cells during vigorous exercise do not get enough oxygen; so glucose is broken down incompletely without oxygen — muscles form lactic acid, and plant cells form ethanol and \(CO_2\). Thus, under low-oxygen conditions, higher plants and animals too perform anaerobic respiration.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Give scientific reason: It is not right to consider the mother responsible for giving birth to a girl child.
solution: The sex of a child is determined by the sex chromosome contributed by the father, not the mother. A woman has \(XX\) sex chromosomes, so all her eggs carry only an X chromosome. A man has \(XY\), so his sperms are of two kinds — X-bearing and Y-bearing. If an X-bearing sperm fertilises the egg, the child is a girl \((XX)\); if a Y-bearing sperm does so, the child is a boy \((XY)\). Since the mother can give only X and it is the father's sperm that decides the sex, it is scientifically wrong to blame the mother for the birth of a girl child.

stem: Give scientific reason: The energy generated from nuclear fuels is not environment friendly.
solution: Nuclear power stations produce highly radioactive waste which remains dangerous for thousands of years and is very difficult to store and dispose of safely. Any leakage of radiation or a reactor accident can cause radiation sickness, cancers, genetic disorders and death of living organisms, and the hot water released causes thermal pollution. Because of this radioactive waste and the risk of radiation hazards, the energy generated from nuclear fuels is not environment friendly.

stem: Complete the following food chain: Grass \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) ____ \(\rightarrow\) Eagle \(\rightarrow\) ____
solution: The completed food chain: Grass \(\rightarrow\) Grasshopper \(\rightarrow\) Frog \(\rightarrow\) Snake \(\rightarrow\) Eagle \(\rightarrow\) Decomposers (microorganisms). Here grass is the producer, the grasshopper is the primary (herbivore) consumer, the frog is the secondary consumer, the snake is the tertiary consumer, the eagle is the top carnivore, and on its death the decomposers (bacteria and fungi) break down the dead matter. (Other acceptable herbivore/carnivore pairs, e.g. insect / lizard, are also valid.)

stem: Distinguish between the following: Class Pisces and Class Reptiles.
solution:
| Class Pisces | Class Reptilia |
|---|---|
| Body is streamlined and covered with mucus-coated scales. | Body is covered with dry, horny, keratinised scales or scutes. |
| Respiration takes place only through gills. | Respiration takes place only through lungs. |
| They are aquatic (live in water). | They are mostly terrestrial (some are aquatic but breathe air). |
| Heart is two-chambered. | Heart is incompletely three-chambered. |
| Fertilization is usually external and eggs are laid in water. | Fertilization is internal and shelled eggs are laid on land. |
Examples: Pisces — Labeo (rohu), Scoliodon; Reptilia — lizard, snake, tortoise.

stem: Observe the following picture and write any two effects of this disaster.
solution: The picture shows a flood (a low-lying area, road and railway track submerged under water with people wading through it). Two effects of a flood: (1) Loss of human and animal life and large-scale damage to houses, crops, roads, railways and other property. (2) Contamination of drinking-water sources leading to the spread of waterborne diseases such as cholera, typhoid and gastroenteritis, along with disruption of transport, electricity and communication.

stem: Write any four methods to reduce stress.
solution: Four methods to reduce stress: (1) Perform regular exercise, yoga, meditation and deep-breathing (pranayama). (2) Take proper rest and adequate sound sleep and eat a balanced, nutritious diet. (3) Engage in hobbies and recreational activities such as music, reading, sports and gardening. (4) Share your problems and feelings with family and friends, and take help/counselling from elders or experts when needed. (Also: proper time management and maintaining a positive attitude.)

stem: Complete the following conceptual picture (uses of 'Sewage after processing' — four uses around the central box).
solution: Uses of sewage (waste water) after processing / treatment: (1) For irrigation of fields in agriculture. (2) For gardening and maintaining green landscapes/parks. (3) For industrial purposes, such as cooling and cleaning in industries and thermal power plants. (4) For recharging groundwater and for non-drinking domestic uses such as flushing toilets, washing and construction work. (Treated water thus conserves fresh water and prevents pollution of rivers.)
